sectionTitles.visitor-refuge: A place for guests to wait

name: Arrakis world

sections.body:
A Fremen settlement grows around the shelter that the desert allows. Rock offers a place for rooms and retreat, while the surrounding sand holds spice and the threat of the Maker. The distance between a safe doorway, a water store and the next work site matters as much as the size of the colony.

Sands of Arrakis builds its survival loop around these conditions: sealed clothing, reclaimed growing beds, finite supplies and deliberate journeys onto the sand.
sections.title: A home beneath the stone

sections.body:
Deep Erg is exposed dune country with little rock and sparse life. Rocky Basin offers broken stone around sheltered sand, making it natural sietch country. Shield Wall provides escarpments, canyon passages and strong defensive positions.

Deep Desert is high-cost travel through Maker country. It can be crossed but does not permit an ordinary colony or settlement. On local maps, genuine rocky substrate offers worm refuge; a constructed floor laid over sand does not.
sections.title: Erg, basin and shield wall

sections.body:
The recommended opening brings three Fremen survivors with stillsuits, reclamation masks, sandwalking skill and finite supplies. Their knowledge makes desert work possible, while their stores give the colony a limited period to establish collection, food and power.

Choose people who can share construction, growing, cooking, tailoring and hauling. Protect food and install the carried condenser early, then develop windtraps and reclaimed beds without spending the entire construction reserve on expansion.
sections.title: The Fremen sietch start

sections.body:
Daily survival and distant opportunity pull the colony in different directions. Water collectors and sheltered workshops support ordinary life; spice runs and trade journeys bring equipment that the sietch cannot make for itself.

Consolidate between expeditions. A larger settlement needs more food, water and repairs, and a profitable trade cannot replace supplies that run out before the caravan returns.

Keep dead animals and human remains out of occupied rooms. Move them to a separate outdoor disposal area or use supported burial and reclamation work. Corpse exposure can cause lung rot; a reclamation mask conserves water but does not grant immunity to corpse-borne illness. Medical work and clean living space matter even when food and water stores are healthy.

Draft defenders when raiders approach. A colonist who fights alone can be overwhelmed and carried away while companions continue sleeping or working. After the fight, stand down, rescue the wounded and tend them before returning everyone to production.

Fire is a separate emergency from desert heat. Keep the home area covered by firefighters and protect the power supply; a burning room can overwhelm normal cooling. Water reserves and an intact shelter help the colony recover after the flames are out.
sections.title: Growing the settlement

sections.body:
Fremen groups include maula scouts, Fedaykin and naibs, alongside ordinary fighters. Imperial levies carry blades and light field clothing, forming small raiding parties before the colony draws more expensive troops. They have modest melee training and no shield or Sardaukar plate. Larger Imperial forces include armored Sardaukar, officers and heavily equipped shield veterans. Elite roles cost more of an encounter’s group budget and are kept out of small early groups.

Fremen desert roles avoid shields, whose emissions are dangerous on exposed sand. Imperial armor and field equipment call for different tactics from an encounter with lightly equipped travelers.
sections.title: People of the desert

sections.body:
House provisioning factors and CHOAM industrial agents maintain reachable trading outposts for supported Fremen colonies. Goodwill, settlement trade and caravan travel govern access. House factors emphasize practical supplies; CHOAM brokers industrial imports and reserved Guild freight.

Guild procurement passes through CHOAM rather than a separate Guild faction. Existing colonies can receive the supported contacts, but a faction that has been destroyed is not brought back.
sections.title: House and CHOAM contacts

sections.body:
A Fremen applicant can ask to join through an accept-or-reject letter. Abandoned freight may offer finite food and materials, while suitable habitat and temperature can bring passing kulon. These opportunities supplement the colony’s work rather than replacing its supply routes.

After a loss, recovery can preserve up to six selected supported Fremen identities, sharing six water rations, four meals and two medicine. Unsupported slots receive a Fremen replacement; without a roster, one survivor is supplied. Emergency assistance adds one Fremen with finite provisions.

Bandit-camp requests require a leader who already shares a supported human enemy with the colony. Broader joiner, resource-pod and wildlife pools remain restricted in the alpha.
sections.title: Visitors, discoveries and recovery

sections.body:
Kulon, Muad’Dib and sand terrapins form the supported native animal roster. Eligible species can appear through migration and self-taming, subject to climate and the usual incident conditions. Kept animals need fodder and physical drinking water; each drink consumes one ration.

An adult female sand terrapin lays an egg about every ten game days, with age and other resource-growth factors affecting the interval. An unfertilized egg provides 0.25 nutrition. With a male, fertilized eggs can hatch after five days at a suitable temperature. This is a slow supplement to food stores.

The supported animals provide no local milk or wool industry. Cloth comes from irrigated fiber and weaving, while specialist textiles are imported.
sections.title: Animals and husbandry

sections.body:
Place sietch meeting markers on genuine worm-safe ground, with a standable approach and no committed Maker hazard. Visitors choose reachable markers; an inaccessible marker does not prevent them from considering another usable one.

A marker directs a visit, not the desert. Ordinary trading duties, pathfinding and active worm hazards still apply, so inspect the route as well as the waiting place.
sections.title: A place for guests to wait

sections.body:
Personal starting possessions are separate from the scenario’s shared stores. In the supported Fremen opening, generated corn becomes Fremen wheat, rice and fungus become pundi rice, and potatoes become Gift to the Thirsty tubers. Physical counts are preserved.

The fungus substitution keeps food value but changes its ingredient and dietary identity. Expanded DLC diets are outside the Core alpha’s supported profile. Existing saved food and unrelated scenarios are not replaced.
sections.title: Personal provisions

sections.body:
The supported setup is Harmony, RimWorld Core and Sands of Arrakis, beginning with the Fremen sietch scenario. The current tested game version is 1.7.4998. The alpha v1 target is November 17, 2026. Its feature list is frozen; this does not mean the release is approved. No DLC is required. Leave Geological Landforms disabled for the supported 1.7 alpha profile. The installed release audited on November 3 declares versions only through 1.6; a compatible release needs separate testing.

Suspensor flight, medical stasis, extra starts and broader species or story additions are outside this alpha. Existing supported production and progression routes remain available.

Some art and sound remain provisional. Save-boundary preservation protects tested living and deceased orphan-relative chains, and a visiting pack-animal drinking loop has been repaired. Campaign testing includes native farming, shelter construction, raid defense, casualty care and recovery after a shelter fire. Keep corpses away from occupied rooms, draft defenders together and rebuild reserves between emergencies. Small Imperial levy raids can now arrive at early threat budgets. These managed test campaigns do not certify every roster, seed or player strategy; broader balance acceptance remains open. The supported research tree uses compact columns with prerequisites to the left and separated buttons that fit the native window vertically. Live review has checked shield controls and clothing across the five native body types and four facings. Audio loading covers the packaged effects and three music tracks; listening and mix acceptance remain in progress. Other DLC and mod combinations have not been established as supported. The project roadmap and repository work packets record the detailed test history.

Private alpha rehearsal packages now include verified file manifests and installation, rollback and known-issues guides. Package verification rejects missing, altered and unexpected files before extraction. This preparation is not public release approval; final listening and player acceptance remain open.
sections.title: Playing the alpha

summary: Arrakis is a world of open erg, sheltered basins and towering rock. Settlement begins where the stone offers refuge; water, spice and the routes between them shape what follows.
